ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image shows two separate outlined figures: a square on the left and an equilateral-looking triangle on the right. There are no side lengths, angle labels, or other measurements marked on either figure. Reasoning: Let the side length of the equilateral triangle be t. Its area is given as 16\sqrt{3}, and the area formula for an equilateral triangle is (\sqrt{3}/4)t^2. So (\sqrt{3}/4)t^2 = 16\sqrt{3}. Dividing by \sqrt{3} gives t^2/4 = 16, so t^2 = 64 and t = 8. The triangle perimeter is 3t = 24. Since the square and triangle have equal perimeters, the square perimeter is also 24, so the square side length is 24/4 = 6. A square diagonal equals side length times \sqrt{2}, so the diagonal is 6\sqrt{2}.
